comparator.name: Organization and Management Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The full-time Dutch-language track requires 60 EC each year. The final year includes 18 EC of electives, a 12 EC team research project and a 12 EC individual thesis. Some courses are taught in English.
components: GROW provides mentoring and personal development across the three years and carries no credits.
Social Psychology for the Social Sciences
The first-year binding study advice threshold is 42 EC from the first-year curriculum.
Choose 18 EC through a minor, free electives or a combination. These credits may be earned at Tilburg or abroad.
In the first semester, small teams carry out qualitative and quantitative research in one or more organisations. Working groups are compulsory.
Bachelor’s Thesis in Organization and Management Studies

The standard spring thesis requires at least 120 EC within the programme. Students conduct individual research with support from a thesis group, complete an AI literacy requirement and defend their thesis.

core: Organisation and management theory, organisational sociology and collaboration within and between organisations
Organisational psychology, human behaviour, leadership and organisational development
Strategy, complex organisational decision-making and management across public and private organisations
Qualitative, quantitative and causal organisational research
Organisational change, advice, intervention and evaluation
adjacent: Innovation, entrepreneurship and responsible organisational change
questions: How do organisations coordinate people, strategy and relationships to function effectively?
How can organisations diagnose, manage and evaluate change?
How can entrepreneurship and innovation support responsible organisational transformation?

candidates.label: Innovation, entrepreneurship and responsible organisational change

selection.assessment: Two options cover the organisation and strategy core and the distinct innovation and entrepreneurship direction. The remaining direct interests are addressed within those options.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Organisations, strategy & human behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: Leadership, organisational psychology, strategy and research form the core, supported by finance and policy analysis.
alternatives.concept: Study how organisations make decisions, coordinate people and manage change. Combine leadership and organisational psychology with negotiation, finance, public policy and social research.
progression: Economics, research methods and introductory leadership prepare for advanced economics, negotiation and organisational psychology. Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation and International Business & Governance.

alternatives.label: Innovation, entrepreneurship & responsible change
alternatives.labelReason: Product design, market research and strategy connect innovation to sustainability and organisational change.
alternatives.concept: Study how organisations develop products and change their practices. Combine design, market research and digital strategy with circular-economy assessment, sustainability governance and stakeholder negotiation.
alternatives.distinctness: This option follows product development, customer research and environmental decisions. The closest option gives more weight to organisational behaviour, social research and public policy.
progression: Product design and sustainability foundations prepare for life-cycle assessment and circular-economy study. Research methods precede marketing and negotiation. Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes advanced business law, strategy and market research.

blocks: Both study accounting and financial decisions. Tilburg also teaches managing projects within and between organisations.
Both introduce economic reasoning about choices, markets and public intervention.
Both use regression to analyse empirical relationships. UCR also teaches instrumental variables and applies the methods to economics.
Both connect survey design, measurement and quantitative analysis. The UCR project studies leadership and social experience.
Both study motivation, teams, leadership and culture in organisations.
Both analyse strategic decisions. UCR focuses on negotiation, bargaining and relationships between parties.
Both use sociological theory to study institutions and social life.
Both use social psychology to study how people act in groups and respond to social influence.
Both introduce social-science research design, measurement and empirical analysis.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection and interpretation. Tilburg applies these skills in its organisation studies sequence.
Both develop statistical analysis of social or behavioural data. UCR also applies multivariable models.
Both study organisational change. UCR focuses on planning for digital transformation.
Both examine entrepreneurship and innovation. UCR develops a venture idea through design and prototyping.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a sequence in organisation theory, strategy, labour law and research methods. It requires both a 12 EC team study in an organisation and a 12 EC individual thesis. The UCR options combine related courses in leadership, strategy, research and responsible innovation.
Tilburg teaches primarily in Dutch and offers some courses in English. UCR teaches in English.

audience.programmeDescription: At Tilburg University, students study how organisations work, make decisions and change. The degree combines sociology, psychology, economics and strategy with research in organisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study in organisational behaviour, strategy and research, or in responsible innovation and entrepreneurship. Tilburg provides dedicated training in labour law, organisational networks and consultancy, and requires both team and individual research projects.
